english.title: Make / possess parking certificate / ID / device with intent to deceive
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) with intent to deceive,

(A)_[made]_
(B)_[had in your possession]_

something so closely resembling an authorisation by way of

(C)_[a certificate]_,
(D)_[a means of identification, namely **(..SPECIFY..)]_,
(E)_[a device, namely **(..SPECIFY..)]_,

as referred to in

(F)_[section 4(2)]_
(G)_[section 4(3)]_
(H)_[section 7(2)]_
(I)_[section 7(3)]_

of the Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984 that it was calculated to deceive.
english.legislation: Contrary to section 115(1)(b) of the Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984 and Schedule 2 to the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Sections 4(2), 4(3), 7(2) and 7(3) of the Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984 relate to traffic regulation orders and orders similar to traffic regulation orders.
(ii) "Calculated to deceive" means "likely to deceive", see R v Davison [1972] 3 All ER 1121

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
